subject: Renewal options: price-hold + conditional credits for next term
messages:
From: Samantha Park <samanthap@cloudlogix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudlogix.com>, procurement@cloudlogix.com
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + capacity needs

Thanks Hannah — quick update from our side. We’re coming up on the anniversary for our Q3 committed pool and procurement asked me to get numbers and a pricing expectation together. Two asks: 1) can Redwood hold the current blended rate for one additional quarter while we firm up a multi-quarter commit? and 2) can you offer a small pool of credits or a refund mechanism for underutilized committed vGPU hours if our forecast misses by >15%?

If those are possible, procurement is comfortable moving fast. Need the high-level in the next 72 hours.

—Samantha
CloudLogix, Sr. Procurement Manager

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samanthap@cloudlogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + capacity needs

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes on a short price-hold and yes to a limited credit construct — but we’ll need to align on commit sizing and a simple true-up trigger.

Two proposal options for your procurement team to consider (high-level):
• 90-day price-hold from current renewal effective date + option to convert to a 12-month recommended commit with a tiered discount schedule (starts at 12% for baseline commit, scales to 18% with +50% capacity).
• Transitional credit pool: allocate up to 10% of annual committed spend as contingent credits that are refundable if actual usage < 85% of committed over the first 2 billing periods; credits apply to future usage.

I’ll loop Ben (pricing lead) and Monica (CS) to flesh the numbers and deliver a formal quote + amendment redline. Expect a formal PDF by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Renewal & Expansion — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: placeholder for formal quote]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: CloudLogix - pricing options and margin check

Hannah / Monica — quick internal note before we send the quote. I ran revenue / margin sims for both options Hannah suggested. Key points:
- 90-day price-hold (no discount change) + 12-month commit conversion: expected blended margin ~42% at baseline commit (good). Upside to 52% if they convert to +50% capacity.
- Transitional credit pool (10% refund cap): conservative exposure ~ $27k over 12 months if they underutilize; acceptable vs. retention risk.

Recommended: propose both options in the external document and highlight the acceleration credit (extra 3% discount if they sign a multi-quarter commit by end of Q2). I’ll attach a price table.

Ben
Sales Manager, Renewals

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudLogix - pricing options and margin check

Adding CS perspective — usage pattern shows a seasonal dip in May/June for CloudLogix; the credit pool helps smooth that. Also recommend: include a 30-day burst buffer (non-committed) to cover spikes without overcommitting. That’s a low-friction add-on.

I’ll draft the language for the amendment around measurement window (monthly buckets, 30-day lookback) and allowable credits.

—Monica

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samanthap@cloudlogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudlogix.com>, procurement@cloudlogix.com
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: CloudLogix renewal options (formal quote attached)

Samantha — attaching two firm options and a short-track amendment to make legal comfortable. Summary below and full quote attached.

Option A — 90-day price-hold then conversion path
• 90-day price hold at current blended rate effective from the renewal date
• Option to convert into a 12-month committed pool within the 90 days; tiered discount: 12% baseline, +4% at +25% capacity, +6% at +50% capacity
• Acceleration bonus: additional 3% off if commitment signed by 30 Jun 2027

Option B — Conditional credit pool + 12-month commit
• 12-month commit at 14% discount (midpoint)
• Transitional credit: Redwood will earmark up to 10% of committed spend as credits refundable to usage if actual utilization < 85% across first two billing cycles; credits apply to subsequent usage or invoice credit at their election
• Included 30-day burst buffer (non-committed) to avoid throttling during spikes

Attachments: CloudLogix_Q3_quote_v3.pdf (pricing table + amendment redline)

If acceptable, we can provision the amendment into DocuSign and start the signature route — I included a DocuSign link in the attachments. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if procurement wants line-by-line.

Best,
Hannah
[Attachment: CloudLogix_Q3_quote_v3.pdf (PDF, 42KB); CLX_Amendment_Redline_v1.docx (Word, 28KB)]

From: Samantha Park <samanthap@cloudlogix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudlogix.com>, procurement@cloudlogix.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudLogix renewal options (formal quote attached)

Thanks for the quick turnaround — both options look reasonable. Procurement asked for two small changes before we route: 1) move the acceleration bonus deadline to 15 Jul (aligns with our finance calendar) and 2) make the credit refund automatic (applied to next invoice) rather than optional.

We’d like the amendment redline updated and the DocuSign packet resent. If Redwood can accept those two items, we’ll push this through legal and sign within 7 business days.

—Samantha
